modern: A man should always have these two rules ready: the first, to do only whatever the reason of the ruling and law-giving faculty may suggest for the good of men; the second, to change your opinion if there is anyone at hand who sets you right and moves you from any opinion. But this change of opinion must come only from a real conviction, as of what is just or of common benefit, and the like, not because it seems pleasant or brings reputation.
original: A man should always have these two rules in readiness; the one to do only whatever the reason of the ruling and legislating faculty may suggest for the use of men; the other, to change thy opinion, if there is any one at hand who sets thee right and moves thee from any opinion. But this change of opinion must proceed only from a certain persuasion, as of what is just or of common advantage, and the like, not because it appears pleasant or brings reputation.
